issues.failure_explanation: Section 3 announces (and the Conclusion repeats) that the scheme maintains discrete counterparts of all listed structural properties including the Gauß law (Remark lem:gauss_law). The paper itself later states the source update does not preserve the Gauß law, and the restart that re-imposes it destroys the proven energy balance; the relaxation variant is never shown to restore both simultaneously. Thus the paper establishes energy balance and admissibility for the split scheme but not simultaneous Gauß-law preservation.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the Section 3 introduction and Conclusion to exclude the Gauß law from the list of preserved properties (or state it is only approximately maintained up to the residual bound of Proposition prop:added-1).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised structure-preservation scope is overstated with respect to the Gauß law; no formal result is affected.
issues.title: Prose claims a discrete Gauß law is maintained, contradicted by Section 4.6
issues.why_classification: Purely a scope statement; a local rewording removes the overclaim without touching any proven result.

issues.failure_explanation: Applying the (correct) polarization identity to the tested equations gives the dissipation term (θ−1/2)[∫ρ|v^{n+1}−v^n|² + α^{-1}∫|∇φ^{n+1}−∇φ^n|²], i.e. coefficient (θ−1/2)/α, whereas both statements write (θ−1/2)/(2α) (equivalently ½ m ρ|Δv|² instead of m ρ|Δv|²). For θ≠1/2 the stated identities are therefore false by a factor 2 in the dissipation term; the fully discrete proposition inherits the same error since its proof 'follows similarly'.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the prefactor (θ−1/2)·1/(2α) by (θ−1/2)·1/α (i.e. (2θ−1)/(2α)) in both statements.
issues.overall_effect: The exact energy identities as stated are wrong for θ=1 (backward Euler); the sign of the dissipation is unaffected, so the energy inequality of cor:added-2 survives.
issues.title: Energy balance dissipation term off by a factor 2 (semi-discrete and fully discrete)
issues.why_classification: A constant-factor correction fixes both identities; the stability conclusion and all downstream inequalities are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: For any constant ψ≡c one has a_{n,θ}(c,c)=0, so the form cannot be coercive on H^1(D) with its norm; coercivity requires restricting to H^1_0 (or a quotient space) via boundary conditions, which are not part of the statement. Moreover the second term equals ∫ρ^n(|∇φ|²+θ²τ²(∇φ·Ω)²)/(1+θ²τ²|Ω|²), which is nonnegative only if ρ^n≥0; the lemma only assumes ρ^n∈L^∞. No proof is given.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the lemma on H^1_0(D) (homogeneous Dirichlet data for the increment) with ρ^n≥0 a.e., and add the two-line proof using the explicit form of B^{-1}.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma as stated is false; its use ('The left-hand side is a coercive operator') in lem:semi_discrete_parabolic_coercive implicitly needs the same missing hypotheses.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
A more careful
  analysis for the case $\theta=1/2$ establishes the improved result

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition is stated as a theorem but its proof reduces the estimate to the assertion that the computed Strang density increment differs from a formal θ-scheme continuity update by O(τ²), and explicitly declares this unverified. The auxiliary 'mass balance' equation also contains a spurious factor α and sign, the operator norm ‖·‖_op is never defined (which dual space), and the improved O(h³+h^{1+s}) claim for θ=1/2 is asserted with no argument at all. The stated bounds are therefore unsupported.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a consistency estimate for the specific hyperbolic solver (for smooth solutions) showing the density increment matches the θ-scheme update to O(τ²), specify the operator norm, and either prove or downgrade the O(h³) claim; alternatively restate the proposition as a conditional/heuristic result.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative claims on Gauß-law drift per step and its telescoped accumulation (cor:added-3), and hence the justification that the restart perturbation is 'small', are unproven.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
This can be achieved via an artificial relaxation approach by lowering the
kinetic energy appropriately~\cite{eulerpoisson23}.

issues.failure_explanation: If δE^{n+1} > E_kin^{n+1} the bracket is negative and the square root undefined, so the update is not well defined in general. Moreover, for the full Euler system only the momentum is rescaled while the conserved total energy E_h^{n+1} is left unchanged, so Σ m E + (2α)^{-1}‖∇φ̃‖² still increases by δE (the rescaling merely converts kinetic into internal energy), contrary to the stated purpose of re-establishing the energy balance; the kinetic energy is also computed with ρ^n rather than the post-Strang density ρ^{n+1}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Clip the ratio at 1 (min(1,·)), use ρ^{n+1} in E_kin, and for the full Euler system update E_i^{n+1} consistently (E ← ε + |m|²/(2ρ) with the rescaled momentum) so the total energy decreases by δE.
issues.overall_effect: The relaxed restart procedure lacks a guarantee of well-definedness and, for the non-barotropic system, does not deliver the claimed restored energy balance.
issues.title: Relaxation restart is ill-defined when δE exceeds kinetic energy and does not adjust total energy
issues.why_classification: Local, routine modifications of the definition restore well-definedness and the intended energy accounting without affecting other results.
